name: red-01-incomplete-bodies-final
purpose: U039 fix 4, RED on the FINAL tests against the retained bytes of the committed server.cjs of commit 146d8f0 (SHA-256 1f7b61fc...; U039_SUBJECT=file:...): the incomplete-body rows (a bad chunk size, a Content-Length body cut by the request timeout, the same then the client's FIN, a missing CRLF after chunk data, a chunk cut by a FIN; behind 0 to 2 complete earlier requests; with and without Expect: 100-continue; HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/1.0; in this process and in a separate server process), the burst of 128 sockets, 8 clients that leave in the middle of a body, the ordering rows with a request in flight and a seeded fuzz. Expected exit 1, every failure an assertion about answers and closed connections (no typed answer, the connection stays open); the five rows that must not change pass. The first RED archive of this item (written at 15:28 local, before server.cjs was edited, against the same retained bytes and the same rows: 99 of 103 tests failed, every one an assertion) is NOT in the repository: its transcripts embed the local user name in every stack trace (controller rule 15). The same command was archived again from a neutral drive letter (S: , a subst of the repository root) with an unchanged copy of the shared recorder that differs in one constant (the repository path), so the paths in the transcripts start with S:/capability; the tests gained one row since (a queued request whose body arrives after its turn began) and the ordering helpers a liveness guard.

notOk: a seeded fuzz of hostile incomplete requests (this process): the earlier reads, at most one typed refusal, a closed connection, nothing applied
the same fuzz against a SEPARATE server process: the process survives, answers afterwards and holds no connection
an incomplete request queued behind a request in flight is dropped after its turn: its handler never runs (no 100 Continue), and the client gets ONE typed refusal
a GET with a broken chunked body queued behind a request in flight answers once, not twice (the handler of the dropped request would refuse the unexpected body again)
the refusal for an incomplete request waits only for the requests before it: [submit in flight][read][incomplete] answers the submit, the read, then the refusal
